items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: Jack was playing first trumpet with Waring's Pennsylvanians

ctx.x: I don't know what for. He had, oh, like seven or eight wives with no divorces, and he used to steal the Western Union boys' bicycles, and he was a thoroughly crazy man, but very talented. Well, I'll give you an example. When we left to go from New York down to Shreveport, Jack was playing first trumpet with Waring's Pennsylvanians, which of course was a very collegiate outfit, and he had been added to the band because Waring was playing at the Roxy Theater, and they had expanded the orchestra to -- you see the…

college band, Waring's Pennsylvanians. You look like a French count or something. Now please take that off." So Jack cut it off, but he also cut every hair on his head off, he shaved his head. So the next show, here comes Waring out in the spotlight and goes bing, bing, and the spotlight comes on Jack, and there he is, bald headed, no moustache, and Waring, said, "Out." And that's how come we happened to go down south.
